description: StormReactor is a Python package from the University of Michigan kLab developers that extends stormwater-quality modelling in EPA SWMM. It supplies pollutant generation and removal methods for network nodes and links, including settling, concentration-dependent removal and completely stirred tank reactors. Users provide a SWMM input file and a Python configuration linking pollutants and assets to treatment parameters. The package updates water-quality states during a PySWMM simulation. Spatial coverage follows the input drainage network, and temporal resolution follows every simulation step. Public source, worked examples and a PyPI package are available free under LGPL-3.0. Reuse includes testing treatment assumptions and water-quality-based control of stormwater infrastructure. A limitation is that the current implementation cannot skip time steps. Node treatment must already be enabled in the SWMM input file before StormReactor can replace it. Existing model-epa-swmm is the underlying model. This review inspected the documented examples without executing them or downloading stormwater observations.
